name: Retinol
summary: A form of vitamin A commonly used in night creams and serums aimed at the look of fine lines and uneven texture.

name: Retinal (retinaldehyde)
summary: A form of vitamin A that is one step closer to retinoic acid than retinol, used in leave-on products for the look of fine lines.

name: Retinyl palmitate
summary: A gentler, ester form of vitamin A often added in small amounts to moisturisers.

name: Hydroxypinacolone retinoate (HPR)
summary: A newer vitamin A ester used in serums as an alternative to retinol.

name: Adapalene
summary: A synthetic retinoid sold as a gel or cream, available without a prescription in some countries and by prescription in others.

name: Glycolic acid
summary: A small alpha hydroxy acid used in exfoliating toners, serums and peels to loosen dead surface cells.

name: Lactic acid
summary: An alpha hydroxy acid that exfoliates the skin surface and is often found in milder exfoliating products.

name: Mandelic acid
summary: An alpha hydroxy acid with larger molecules than glycolic acid, used in exfoliating serums and peels.

name: Gluconolactone
summary: A polyhydroxy acid used for gentle exfoliation in products made for skin that dislikes stronger acids.

name: Lactobionic acid
summary: A polyhydroxy acid used for mild exfoliation and as a moisture-binding ingredient.

name: Salicylic acid
summary: An oil-soluble beta hydroxy acid used in cleansers and treatments for oily or clogged-looking skin.

name: L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C)
summary: The pure form of vitamin C, used in serums as an antioxidant; it breaks down easily when exposed to air and light.

name: Sodium ascorbyl phosphate
summary: A water-soluble, more stable derivative of vitamin C used in lightweight serums and creams.

name: Magnesium ascorbyl phosphate
summary: A water-soluble, stable derivative of vitamin C found in gentler vitamin C products.

name: Ascorbyl glucoside
summary: Vitamin C bound to a sugar molecule to make it more stable in water-based formulas.

name: Ascorbyl tetraisopalmitate
summary: An oil-soluble vitamin C derivative used in creams and oil-based serums.

name: 3-O-ethyl ascorbic acid
summary: A stable vitamin C derivative that dissolves in both water and oil, used in serums.

name: Niacinamide
summary: A form of vitamin B3 used in serums and moisturisers for the look of uneven tone and visible pores.

name: Benzoyl peroxide
summary: An antibacterial, peeling ingredient used in washes and gels made for blemish-prone skin; it can bleach fabric.

name: Azelaic acid
summary: A dicarboxylic acid used in creams and gels for blemish-prone and redness-prone skin.

name: Sulfur
summary: A mineral long used in masks and spot treatments for oily, blemish-prone skin.

name: Tranexamic acid
summary: An amino acid derivative used in serums aimed at the look of dark patches and uneven tone.

name: Kojic acid
summary: A by-product of fungal fermentation used in products aimed at the look of dark spots; it can irritate sensitive skin.

name: Alpha-arbutin
summary: A plant-inspired, hydroquinone-related ingredient used in serums aimed at the look of dark spots.

name: Urea
summary: A moisture-binding ingredient naturally present in skin, used in rich creams, especially for dry or rough areas.

name: Hyaluronic acid
summary: A water-attracting molecule used in serums and moisturisers to help skin feel plumper and more hydrated.

name: Ferulic acid
summary: A plant antioxidant often paired with vitamin C in serums to help keep the formula stable.

name: Tocopherol (vitamin E)
summary: An oil-soluble form of vitamin E used as an antioxidant and conditioning ingredient in creams and oils.
